subject: POC / Trial planning - workload & success criteria (AcmeHealth)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: POC / Trial planning - workload & success criteria (AcmeHealth)

Hi Alice / Tom - great to meet you both today. Thanks for the demo and the detailed explanations of your priority use cases. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum for the POC/trial:

Summary of what we heard (please correct any mistakes):
- Primary use case: clinical intake summarization + triage for downstream workflows (risk scoring, routing).
- Key flows: short intake notes (avg 40-60 tokens) and longer discharge summaries (~800-2,400 tokens) for batch reranking.
- Current traffic expectation: daytime steady traffic with occasional after-hours bursts.

Requested from you: workload profile + success criteria so we can size the Dedicated/Trial environment and produce an evaluation plan. Specifically we need: RPS, typical prompt/response token lengths, concurrency, burst-pattern examples, and any SLAs you need (P95 latency target, availability).

Proposed POC objectives / success criteria (draft):
1) Latency: 95th percentile generation latency <= 400ms for short intake (<=150 tokens) under baseline concurrency (see numbers below).
2) Throughput: sustain 60 RPS for short flows and process batch job of 10k long documents overnight while keeping SLA for short flows.
3) Accuracy: maintain parity (no more than 3% regression) on your clinical extraction eval set compared to your existing in-house baseline.
4) Stability: no failures or degraded performance during two simulated burst windows (see schedule).

Proposed evaluation plan & timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): exchange workload profile + access + NDA / security checklist items.
- Week 1: Redwood provision trial instance + ingest sample data; run smoke tests.
- Week 2: Execute throughput/latency tests and run your evaluation prompts; produce results and tuning recommendations.
- Week 3: Joint review, iterate on prompts/config; decision point on Dedicated vs. production rollout.

Ownership:
- Redwood: Ben (sales) + Dylan (solutions/benchmarks) + Marissa (CS onboarding).
- AcmeHealth: Alice (product lead) + Tom (platform/infra).

Baseline numbers (please confirm):
- Expected steady RPS: 40 RPS (short-intake)
- Peak burst RPS: 250 RPS sustained for ~5-10 minutes during spikes
- Typical prompt tokens: 20-120 tokens
- Typical response tokens (short flows): 30-200 tokens
- Long document tokens (batch): 800-2,400 tokens
- Concurrent active sessions: 150 typical, up to 600 during spikes

Next steps: can you send the workload_profile.csv (or equivalent) and confirm the success criteria above? If it's easier, Tom, can we schedule a quick 30-min call Wed or Thu for the traffic/infra questions?

Thanks,
Ben

Subject: Re: POC / Trial planning - workload & success criteria (AcmeHealth)

Thanks Ben - great recap and aligned on most points. Attaching a simple workload_profile.csv with the numbers you requested (sampled from last 30 days). High level answers inline below and in the CSV.

Workload profile (confirmed):
- Steady-state RPS (short-intake): 45 RPS (weekdays 08:00-18:00)
- Typical daytime concurrency: ~160 active sessions
- Peak bursts: single-region marketing emails and release windows cause spikes up to 300 RPS lasting 3-12 minutes; we also see multi-hour elevated traffic during population health jobs (rare).
- Typical prompt/response distribution: short prompts median 60 tokens; short responses median 120 tokens; long batch docs average 1,400 tokens.
- Tokenization: we use UTF-8 text with no binary artifacts; average tokens per word ~1.3 given medical shorthand.

Success criteria - priority order:
1) Reliability: 99.9% of requests complete successfully during normal operations and during one simulated spike event.
2) Latency: P95 <= 400ms for short flows (<=150 response tokens) under baseline steady-state concurrency.
3) Accuracy: match or improve our current entity extraction precision (we can share a small eval set).

Constraints / compliance notes:
- We must run the trial in a VPC-connected environment (traffic never leaves our VPC for inference requests).
- SOC2 and penetration test artifacts will be required before a production rollout.

Attaching: workload_profile.csv (CSV, 3 pages) with minute-level RPS samples, token length histograms, and concurrency snapshots.

Alice Gomez
Senior Product Manager, AcmeHealth
alice.gomez@acmehealth.com

[attachment: workload_profile.csv (text/csv)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC / Trial planning - workload & success criteria (AcmeHealth)

Perfect - thanks for the CSV and the clarifications, Alice. Based on what's in the profile we've drafted a POC configuration and timeline. Summary below; happy to adjust.

POC configuration (draft):
- Environment: VPC-connected trial instance (private control plane) configured with 4 dedicated GPU workers for steady throughput, burst autoscale to 12 workers for short spikes.
- Batching policy: continuous batching with 50ms max latency budget for short flows; KV prefix caching enabled for repeated prompts.
- Quantization: recommend int8 quantized model for batch/throughput testing to reduce token cost; we'll validate quality on your eval set.

Planned tests & ownership:
- Day 1 (provision): Redwood stands up VPC trial and shares connectivity docs - owner: Marissa.
- Day 2 (ingest + smoke): Redwood ingests sample data, run smoke tests - owner: Dylan.
- Day 4 (steady-state test): Run 60-minute steady-state at 45 RPS with 160 concurrency; measure P50/P95/P99 latencies - owner: Dylan + Tom.
- Day 5 (burst tests): Two scheduled bursts: 300 RPS for 10 minutes and a 10-minute elevated 200 RPS test; measure error rates and fallback behavior - owner: Dylan + Tom.
- Day 7 (batch job): Run overnight batch job of 10k long docs (avg 1,400 tokens) and measure throughput/cost - owner: Redwood bench team.

Deliverables by end of POC:
- Latency and error-rate report by route/model
- Cost estimate for steady-state and peak profiles (tokens and infra)
- Tuning recommendations (batch/quantization/model pairing)
- Joint decision checklist (meet next Weds to review results)

Questions / asks before we provision:
1) Can your infra team provide a small AWS VPC peering or PrivateLink contact for Marissa to work with? (tom@acmehealth? please loop them into the VPC onboarding ticket)
2) Can you confirm the eval set location or share it to the drive link above?

If that looks good I'll get the provisioning ticket started and propose Wed 08/13 at 10am PT for a call to review connectivity details.

Thanks again - Ben
